# Canvas ports and further ideas

The 27 baseline ports retain archived proportions, palette and manifest traits in Canvas-owned compositions. They don't relink old CSS, register every port in ordinary builds or establish perceptual acceptance. Settings offers Studio, Obsession Mode and Cartridge Quest; Axis Break, Tideplot, Counterform Choir, Aftergarden and Vesperfold are outside this cohort.

The recorded detail pass adds code-native materials, actual focus/selection/playback treatment and mini companions. No effect may invent tempo, format, device or analysis facts. [The measurements](CANVAS_THEME_PORT_BASELINE_EVIDENCE.md) explain stock layouts. Each paragraph marked “Proposed” below is still an idea, even where a related control already exists.

## Dev Lab

Dev Lab keeps Studio's layout and swaps the accent colors to make a test window easy to recognize. A diagnostic grid and test labels sit behind the ordinary controls. Cyan marks playback, and the outline follows whichever module has focus.

Proposed: An optional diagnostic ribbon and focus-resolved boundaries could show actual component state. A deterministic control/long-label/empty-state workspace would help compare it without adding developer noise.

## Orbital Retro-Future

Clipped panels and concentric lines make this look like a spacecraft console. Cyan and gold edges separate the instruments, while the transport's orbit appears during playback. The library still uses a familiar linear list.

Proposed: Progress could use one orbital sweep, with queue-depth rings, brief confirmed-action ticks and original format/device readouts. Keep browsing readable rather than turning it into a dial.

## Bulkhead Terminal

Inset steel panels, scanlines and hazard textures give the console some weight. Buttons move two pixels when pressed. Compact type and closely grouped controls suit the equipment, provided the track list stays readable.

Proposed: Further work could distinguish armed/requested/confirmed actions, show queue position on an original strip and use restrained playback vibration. A damaged-terminal empty state still needs obvious recovery.

## Graphite Loadout

Graphite panels sit on a measured grid, with clipped bays and thin lime or cyan edges. Keyboard and pointer focus emphasize the bay in use. The recorded pass kept the equipment feel without adding a second set of controls.

Proposed: Bays could emphasize the active function, with a slow tagged-BPM cadence, literal device/format engravings and a compact transition inspector. Crossfade state must come from an implemented source.

## Obsession Mode

Most of the player stays near black, with large condensed titles and a small amount of crimson. The earlier pass used a red line and selection frame to suggest a thriller poster. The later reconstruction below changes how that mark follows the listener's attention.

The later reconstruction replaces fixed seams with one attended-object mark: confirmed playback outranks selection, then focus. Open/solid form separates intent and playback. Local play counts drive four coarse title-pressure bands without a displayed number. The mechanic stays shared, motion-off has its own composition, and the two existing assets keep their provenance.

Proposed: a resting mark for an empty collection, aspect-aware cropping, collection pressure only after a collection play total has an owner, and static specimens of every state before more motion.

## Crystal Audio

Lilac edges and layered glass surround the artwork. Light patterns remain inside the panels, and the color becomes slightly stronger during playback. Cover Flow handles browsing; the soft shapes and slow movement shouldn't make the controls harder to find.

Proposed: Artwork color could feed bounded caustics behind controls. A real energy signal could affect waterlight, with separate selection/output facets, original missing-art placeholders and a reduced-motion equivalent.

## Neon Burst

Halftone dots, fluorescent edges and offset shadows make the player resemble a blacklight print. Pressing a control shifts its printed layers. The linear library stays readable against the dark field.

Its reconstruction uses one --nb-slip scalar across surfaces, reaching zero only for confirmed playback. Tagged BPM through flowTempoValue maps (bpm - 55) / 145 into an 8–15px halftone pitch; untagged tracks use a fixed line screen and explicit untagged state. It updates on confirmed track change, with no keyframes. October 3 work contained hover/focus/press and utility reveals, shortened the hero and removed inherited cartridge captions. It declares no assets. Local selector/shop tests don't establish paid delivery or packaged availability.

Proposed: Later ideas include actual collection tempo coverage, an editor link from an untagged state, a device-change plate once that input exists, and static specimens across selection/playback/drag/failure/empty states.

## Monument

Warm stone, raised paper panels and collection labels make room for the album art. A slate mark identifies the playing track. The carousel and mostly still layout suit looking through albums without much decoration moving around them.

Proposed: The current album could receive a literal collection label, with quiet lighting and accessible queue-change confirmation. Stone, bronze and paper variants should keep the same state meanings.

## Analog Dossier

The player resembles a set of listening records: ruled paper, red margins, cabinet-like panels and catalog labels. A double line identifies the playing track. Short mechanical responses fit the filing-room idea better than drifting panels.

Proposed: A keyboard-accessible folder reveal, original action stamps, provenance annotations and optional paper sounds could extend the filing language without obscuring failures.

## Cosmic Cinema

A sparse star field surrounds a dark central stage, with silver instrument edges and an orbit around the transport during playback. The carousel keeps the collection close to the artwork. Later work added the compact readouts described below.

October 3 work added Space Grotesk, orbital shortcuts and a compact strip of actual playback/source/rate/depth/tempo/queue/progress facts. Stable-footprint disclosure and a shorter hero protect browsing space. The mini uses matching type and the existing original missing-art halo. Local free selector tests didn't add a built-in registration.

Proposed: Queue previews could orbit a stable current track. Duration/progress could shape a contained lens arc, with a short aperture response and original source/output readouts; text must remain undistorted.

## Frosted Void

Dark glass and thin spectral edges frame the music. Frost clears around the area in use without covering its contents. The material can remain atmospheric, but text and controls still need enough contrast without relying on the effect.

Proposed: Possible work includes focus-cleared frost, one artwork-colored film edge, restrained playback bubble tension and a high-contrast version that doesn't depend on transparency.

## Obsidian Glass

Rounded black panels use layered depth, narrow cyan edges and small reflections. The active row or control gets an inner light. Slow movement is part of the design, with a still version needed for ordinary use.

Proposed: Keep later edge lighting and artwork color narrow. Panel settling needs an immediate reduced-motion equivalent, with a clear high-contrast/lower-cost material option.

## Dead Signal

The remaining direction is an old broadcast receiver: dark panels, bone-colored text and a cyan trace. Crimson identifies missing media. The former metal, tower and tape artwork was retired; the next version needs its own assets and layout.

October 3 retired the old decorative images and Oswald font pending redesign. Earlier worn-shutter, scratched-metal, tower and tape treatments are historical, not bundled assets. Palette, code-defined geometry and shared sound behavior remain.

Proposed: A later rebuild could use a narrow trace for real buffering, a distinct unavailable-media state and original archive/transmitter marks. Any tuning transition needs limits for flashing and motion sensitivity.

## Meme Machine

Dark channels, blurple edges and a message-like playing row borrow the familiarity of a group chat. The reading column stays clean even when the surrounding colors and reactions are playful. Browsing remains a linear list.

Proposed: Original reactions could follow actual playback events, and queue changes could read like local bot messages. Repeated comedy needs a calm control; jokes must leave metadata and recovery visible.

## Cartridge Quest

A beveled console frame surrounds the library, with pixel-cut corners, a gold deck edge and green playback marks. Buttons have a small amount of travel. The later reconstruction develops the cartridge and save-file organization rather than loading the old stylesheet.

The later reconstruction restores cartridge/save-file organization, title-screen stage, pause/route/achievement cabinets, roster queue, real progress and local XP/run/high-score/combo, plus import/encounter feedback, output hardware, optional sounds and the CQ-16 mini deck. It reuses the recorded local art without loading the retired stylesheet.

Proposed: Later work could allow local save-slot names and editable playlist chapter titles, plus a keyboard-first roster after stable reorder receipts exist. Static encounter/error/empty states should precede more effects.

## Sakura Bloom

Paper panels, a lacquered player deck and a few fixed blossom marks give this a quiet room-like feel. Sage highlights the playing track. Soft controls and slow movement leave the linear library easy to use.

Proposed: A sparse branch field, lacquer controls and one seasonal track-change gesture could extend the room. Any energy response needs a real signal and an equally legible still composition.

## Lo-Fi Café

Walnut rails frame a paper listening area, with small order labels and moss-green playback marks. The stage edge warms during playback. The reconstruction below gives paper, rain and saved collections their own behavior.

Its reconstruction keeps the wood fixed while paper responds. Explicitly chosen collections use bounded durable cafeAnchors; play wear uses actual play counts/history. With history capped at 200, a missing surviving date says “last time not recorded.” Rain follows playback behind the wood, and local-hour lamp warmth changes only glow at confirmed track changes. Queue tickets retain real drag/focus, and the two CC0 photos keep their provenance.

Proposed: A separate set-aside list needs semantics of its own before the proposed Collector's Table density. Artwork tint must preserve ink contrast. Room tone would be an audio feature with mute/routing, not CSS decoration.

## ASCII Social

A character grid and inset window frames recall an older desktop media player. Local labels, a cyan playback mark and a dashed focus cursor keep its state visible. The character art stays separate from ordinary text and the linear track list.

Proposed: Characters could become restrained meters and separators, with a focus cursor that respects text editing. Deterministic local notices and compact/spacious layouts should avoid fake network activity.

## Poster Pop

Three-color paper panels, ink shadows and a slightly skewed green playing sticker give the layout the feel of a pasted-up flyer. Large type and soft controls carry the identity. Brief pressed and hover responses should leave the track list stable.

Proposed: Bounded artwork color and distinct saved/queued/playing stickers could extend the flyer. Paste-up transitions need a still alternative and a print-safe high-contrast version.

## Creator Layer

Graphite panels and blurple channel edges make a compact companion window. Small local labels keep it glanceable, and a green tally follows actual playback. It doesn't imply that a microphone or stream is connected.

Proposed: A broadcast-safe now-playing card needs privacy controls. Mic/stream status must wait for real integrations. A second-monitor density and accessible tally language could keep facts glanceable.

## Modular Signal

Lavender and blush blocks sit against black outlines and offset shadows. The square modules show their editable boundaries while Canvas composition mode is active. Outside editing, those outlines don't need to compete with the music.

Proposed: Bounded rearrangement and paths ending at the real output could develop the modular idea. Insertion/removal motion should follow actual workspace changes, with plain loading/empty/unavailable modules.

## Cut Sheet

Ruled paper, terracotta margins and circular groove marks make the player resemble a session sheet. A contained texture responds to playback. The references to mastering are visual; they don't describe the source recording or imply mastering tools.

Proposed: Timing-backed transition annotations, reversible EQ pencil marks and a restrained progress groove could fit the sheet. Exportable session notes need a data/privacy contract first.

## Acid Transit

Magenta and lime lines connect clipped panels like stops on a night route. A line identifies the playing queue item. The holographic edge and short mechanical responses stay around the controls rather than washing over the library.

Proposed: A queue line could distinguish current, next, skipped and unavailable items, with one progress marker. Temporary access tape clears with its mode; delay/reroute metaphors need actual buffering or edits.

## Ghost Index

Bone-colored grid lines and faint traces sit behind the archive-like library. Coral follows focus, while a stable green mark identifies playback. Spectral Field supplies the browsing interaction; the atmosphere must leave that interaction readable.

Proposed: Focus could resolve nearby traces and metadata-derived specimen glyphs. Keep coral intent separate from green confirmed playback, including a static indexed layout without atmospheric motion.

## Violet//Violent

Offset transparent layers frame each object. Violet marks what the listener is choosing, and cyan marks confirmed playback. Memory Cascade carries the layered objects through the library, with the same distinction in the mini-player.

Proposed: Later work could clarify remembered context, intent and playback across panels, with bounded short-lived optical history. Beat effects require trusted analysis; offsets/contrast should carry the still version.

## Abyssal Press

Cream-edged plates and ocean-like pressure bands surround the current track. Magenta marks browsing and cyan marks playback. Pressure Stack compresses neighboring entries without changing which track is actually playing.

Proposed: Queue depth could form pressure bands around a stable current track. Real loudness/spectral input could emboss one field away from text, with controlled transitions and original literal labels.

## Harmonic Registry

Light paper, ruled lines and black frames make the library resemble a specimen book. Violet marks a choice; a separate cyan mark identifies playback. The linear list leaves room for relationships between tracks without presenting a guess as a musical fact.

Proposed: Families could suggest relationships without claiming objective compatibility. Key/BPM displays need provenance and uncertainty; comparison sheets must leave the chosen queue path obvious and reversible.
